steps.name: Sarkaz Worker A
steps.text: Slow down! You got a death wish or something? We're carrying a damned Originium plate! We're all dead if you drop it!

steps.name: Sarkaz Worker A
steps.text: Seriously, what the hell is wrong with this family, using this as a pickling stone? Do they like their pickles with a touch of Originium?

steps.name: Sarkaz Worker B
steps.text: Shut your *Sarkaz expletive* mouth and keep moving.

steps.name: Sarkaz Worker B
steps.text: We gotta clear this whole district before the end of the day, unless you want the overseer to chew our heads off after the Lich chews his.

steps.name: Sarkaz Worker A
steps.text: So many houses, and we got to clean every single speck of Originium off 'em... doesn't Babel have a dedicated construction team? Why don't we just tear it all down and rebuild from scratch?

steps.name: Sarkaz Worker A
steps.text: Say, it's gonna take some getting used to, not having any Originium around.

steps.name: Sarkaz Worker B
steps.text: I said, shut your *Sarkaz expletive* mouth.

steps.name: Sarkaz Worker B
steps.text: We didn't have a choice but to rely on the mines. Now that Kazdel doesn't need to worry about energy anymore, of course we gotta clean house...

steps.name: Sarkaz Worker B
steps.text: Unless you LIKE living in a den of Originium—hey, watch where you're going, Lich!

steps.name: Sarkaz Worker A
steps.text: Keep your threads tucked away, Lich. Who knows what might happen if they got tied up in the Originium...
That's not very polite.

steps.name: Ermengarde
steps.text: You can cut the threads with your horns if they do get tied up. But who knows what dimension my thread will drag you into, if it comes to that?

steps.name: Ermengarde
steps.text: Alright, I don't think I should scare you any further, gentlemen. Go ahead.

steps.name: Sarkaz Worker A
steps.text: Did I imagine it? What's that light?

steps.name: Sarkaz Worker B
steps.text: It came from the house up there, maybe? Let's take a look.

steps.name: Ermengarde
steps.text: ...I'll go.

steps.name: Sarkaz Worker A
steps.text: Wha?

steps.name: Ermengarde
steps.text: Those houses are right by the agricultural plate that has just been integrated. The light must be from one of the soil beacons, in reaction to the Originium plate that you're carrying.

steps.name: Ermengarde
steps.text: If Wiš'adel finds out the farmland that she's spent two years cultivating got polluted...

steps.name: Sarkaz Worker B
steps.text: Alright. Let's get outta here.

steps.name: Cecelia
steps.text: D-Don't come any closer!

steps.name: Ezell
steps.text: Ugh...
Ermengarde looks at the agitated girl standing in front of her, trying to shield the man behind her with her tiny body.
It's a Sankta man, kneeling feebly on the ground. His halo and wings have shattered, their pieces still trembling and flickering, like dying fireflies.
The Sankta does not speak. It is as though he has fallen into a deep slumber.

steps.name: Cecelia
steps.text: Who are you? Are you here to take us away?
The girl is all tensed up. Ermengarde bends down and puts her hands on her knees, doing her best to show that she intends no harm, even wagging her energized tail friendly.

steps.name: Ermengarde
steps.text: I mean no harm, young lady.

steps.name: Ermengarde
steps.text: I sent the other Sarkaz away. Did you heard that? Maybe I can help you... help him.
Ermengarde closes the door behind her, shutting out any prying eyes.
She adjusts her hat. Invisible threads reach out through an unknowable dimension.

steps.name: Ermengarde
steps.text: Master.

steps.name: Fremont
steps.text: All that red-tape and long-winded tomes in the spires made me sick, but I should thank the twin sheep for their hospitality, compared to what I have to deal with now.

steps.name: Fremont
steps.text: Every policy has to be communicated verbally, and you have to explain things over and over again. When are we going to implement basic education for government employees?

steps.name: Ermengarde
steps.text: This is urgent.

steps.name: Fremont
steps.text: ...Go ahead.

steps.name: Ermengarde
steps.text: I'm at the furnace node. I found two Sanktas with broken halos... one of them doesn't look right at all.

steps.name: Fremont
steps.text: Bring them here. Try not to let anyone see you. We don't need a scene in the streets.

steps.name: Fremont
steps.text: I'll go wake Wiš'adel. Looks like it's time for our Speaker to speak at an emergency meeting.

steps.name: Ewigegnade
steps.text: ...The list is a long one.

steps.name: Ewigegnade
steps.text: You're saying that all forty-three Sanktas stationed at spires across Zwillingstürme have abandoned their posts without permission.

steps.name: Michael
steps.text: Yes, Ewigegnade.

steps.name: Michael
steps.text: They have already left Leithanian soil, forcing their way through the checkpoint at the Erdenherre border.

steps.name: Ewigegnade
steps.text: Leithanien took in these errari as an act of kindness. Now they have chosen desertion... without any warning.

steps.name: Michael
steps.text: Not entirely.

steps.name: Michael
steps.text: The night watch of the Reichsmusikhochschule witnessed a Sankta scholar leaving, and noted that his halo and wings were shattered, as if there was a... serious accident.

steps.name: Ewigegnade
steps.text: A Fallen?

steps.name: Michael
steps.text: The symptoms do not align exactly.

steps.name: Ewigegnade
steps.text: How do you think this should be dealt with?

steps.name: Michael
steps.text: A-Are you asking for my opinion?

steps.name: Ewigegnade
steps.text: Of course I am.

steps.name: Ewigegnade
steps.text: You are the mouth of the Austere Authority, Michael Wolfgang.

steps.name: Ewigegnade
steps.text: You are the only one who can speak with her voice in this realm, besides me.

steps.name: Michael
steps.text: Well...

steps.name: Ewigegnade
steps.text: You've grown in the past few years, both physically and mentally. Hildegard has taught you well.

steps.name: Ewigegnade
steps.text: I must commend you for making the report that you just did.

steps.name: Ewigegnade
steps.text: You have, in effect, admitted that you have access to certain... exceptional channels.

steps.name: Michael
steps.text: The Sanktas of Leithanien have fallen and deserted en masse. This is a serious matter... you are the only one capable of dealing with it, Ewigegnade.

spans.text: The Sanktas of Leithanien have fallen and deserted
. This is a serious matter... you are the only one capable of dealing with it, Ewigegnade.

steps.name: Ewigegnade
steps.text: I know that you, the Urtica boy, and even that Gräfchen are doing a few things under the surface. As a reward, I'm willing to turn a blind eye to that.

spans.text: I know that you, the Urtica boy, and even that
are doing a few things under the surface. As a reward, I'm willing to turn a blind eye to that.

steps.name: Ewigegnade
steps.text: Now, back to the topic at hand.

steps.name: Michael
steps.text: The border guard reports that they seem to be headed for Laterano. It's likely that the Lateran Curia is involved.

steps.name: Michael
steps.text: Shall we send the Empresses' Voice to confront the Curia?

steps.name: Ewigegnade
steps.text: One year ago, after Das Kaiserinnensfest, Yvangelista XI communicated to me that he wishes to work hand-in-hand with Leithanien.

steps.name: Ewigegnade
steps.text: The anomalous circumstances with the Sanktas may indicate that the calamity the Pope had feared, so much that he would seek our help, has come at last.

steps.name: Ewigegnade
steps.text: Issue an edict, in the name of Eternal Grace and Austere Authority, to summon the best casters and scholars among all the spires.

steps.name: Ewigegnade
steps.text: Calamity will spare no corner of this great land. We must hasten our studies into the secret retrieved from the chaos.

steps.name: Michael
steps.text: Yes, Your Majesty.

steps.name: Michael
steps.text: I will arrange for it at once.

steps.name: Ewigegnade
steps.text: Perhaps not entirely at once.

steps.name: Michael
steps.text: Wh-What I mean is, I will instruct the Empresses' Voice to...

steps.name: Ewigegnade
steps.text: The eventide is beautiful tonight, Michael. Stay and enjoy it with me.

steps.name: Ewigegnade
steps.text: The wound in the sky has healed. She would have appreciated this too... would she not?

steps.name: Aurela
steps.text: Tsk...

steps.name: Voice in the Tent
steps.text: ...East of the east of La Unidad, Laterano, holy city of white♪

steps.name: Voice in the Tent
steps.text: The guns there shoot fireworks, the targets all apples♪

steps.name: Voice in the Tent
steps.text: When we pray sincere, He gives us bread♪

steps.name: Voice in the Tent
steps.text: When we seek salvation, He sets us free♪

steps.name: Aurela
steps.text: Sing, sing until you're asleep.

steps.name: Aurela
steps.text: The god in your dreams is kinder than Laterano's.

steps.name: Nueda
steps.text: You didn't need to go this far on the night watch, Aurela.

steps.name: Aurela
steps.text: ...Get lost.

steps.name: Aurela
steps.text: This is the Minoan border. Those Singas nobles won't go any further. You're safe.

steps.name: Aurela
steps.text: The abbey is no more. We go our separate ways.

steps.name: Nueda
steps.text: Ten years ago, you came to my abbey and protected my plate from those nobles without a word. Now, you're leaving without a word.

steps.name: Aurela
steps.text: You preach your teachings, I protected the kids in exchange for a new roof over my head, that's all.

steps.name: Aurela
steps.text: Don't think too much of yourself.

steps.name: Nueda
steps.text: You can't leave, Aurela.

steps.name: Nueda
steps.text: I'm not asking.

steps.name: Nueda
steps.text: Our destination is the same. We'll go with you to Laterano.

steps.name: Aurela
steps.text: And when did I say I was bringing you with me?

steps.name: Nueda
steps.text: We've been together for ten years. It's a long time for a K'uk'ulkan.

steps.name: Nueda
steps.text: Maybe I don't trust Laterano that much. But I do trust you.

steps.name: Nueda
steps.text: The Lateran stripped you of citizenship, and you've cursed the city many times while I sang the hymns...

steps.name: Nueda
steps.text: But look at yourself. After all these years in Bolívar, you still won't take off the gun-knight's armor...

steps.name: Nueda
steps.text: Even though you've fallen, lost the ability to wield a patron firearm, you somehow got your hands on this Blacksteel gun, which means you never—

steps.name: Aurela
steps.text: Shut up.
The fallen angel suddenly raises her gun, the muzzle almost reaching the K'uk'ulkan's lips.

steps.name: Aurela
steps.text: If you trust me, you should remember that I've told you many times the Holy City is not so friendly, kind, or tolerant as you imagine...

steps.name: Aurela
steps.text: Half the people who followed you from the abbey are not Sankta.

steps.name: Aurela
steps.text: There are plenty of places you can go after leaving Bolívar.

steps.name: Nueda
steps.text: Perhaps what we follow is not the true Lateran faith, but it's what kept a modicum of order in our lives amidst the chaos of Bolívar.

steps.name: Nueda
steps.text: There's no way I can convince the others to go somewhere else. They want to make the pilgrimage.

steps.name: Nueda
steps.text: Nor can I convince myself. Laterano is part of us now, after these long years.

steps.name: Aurela
steps.text: You've got to be kidding.

steps.name: Nueda
steps.text: Think of the Sanktas in the abbey. They've never known Laterano, only the trauma of the Fall.

steps.name: Nueda
steps.text: Only by returning to Laterano will they know what happened. Only then will the fear be driven out. Only then can their 'sickness' be cured.

steps.name: Nueda
steps.text: Let us walk together for a little while longer, Aurela.

steps.name: Aurela
steps.text: I'm not going back to Laterano because I miss home.

steps.name: Aurela
steps.text: Ten years ago, an old man said something like this to me, at another abbey. He was the one who exiled me in the name of Laterano, because of some silly mistake.

steps.name: Aurela
steps.text: He wanted to hear me repent, hear me pray. He said there was a chance I could go back, if I truly, sincerely repented for my sins...

steps.name: Nueda
steps.text: You refused?

steps.name: Aurela
steps.text: I sure did.

steps.name: Aurela
steps.text: Something seems to have gone really wrong in the Holy City. I'm going to seize this chance for revenge.
Nueda steps forward, and presses her face against the cold gun barrel.

steps.name: Nueda
steps.text: We won't stop you.

steps.name: Nueda
steps.text: We just need a guide. Someone who knows the way.

steps.name: Nueda
steps.text: Someone like you.
The hymns begin to die down, replaced by the sound of children crying out.
Aurela lets out a laugh and puts away her gun.
The Shrine of Nurtury smears its colors on the surrounding buildings, opening numerous portals through which strange creatures with halos emerge one-by-one, falling to the ground.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Did those things get the blessing of Laterano too? It wasn't just the baby arborbeast?

steps.name: Enlightened Creature A
steps.text: (Claps excitedly)

steps.name: Enlightened Creature B
steps.text: (Sways uncertainly)
They crawl on the ground, wagging their heads furiously, still trying to adjust to their halos. They bellow in a low, rhythmic voice, as if joining together in prayer.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Urgh. That's one ugly, chaotic voice of the heart.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: If everyone in the Holy City has fallen into a sort of mass hallucination of an unknown source...

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Does this scene before us mean that the boundary between reality and falsehood is being blurred, and that Laterano is being invaded by a material threat?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: This is even more incomprehensible than what we experienced in the Pavillon.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: One of them has noticed us, Fede.

steps.name: Enlightened Creature A
steps.text: (Praying)

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: The noise we made seems to have disrupted their ritual.
An enlightened creature turns toward Federico and Arturia, perhaps because it missed part of the prayer.
Its halo flashes, and its bloated hide seems to grow light and lithe, approaching the duo at high speed.
Federico raises his gun, but the halo-adorned creature pays no heed, not even stopping its prayer.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Fall back. The nature of these creatures is yet unknown. We must not be surrounded.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: I thought you would shoot without hesitation.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Are these creatures our kin, Fede? Are you in violation of the Law if you shoot?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Is that a joke, or simply an ill-timed curiosity?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Your patron firearm is lost, and I can neutralize these creatures without discharging mine.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: We will determine whether they should be considered our kindred, but not now.

spans.text: determine whether they should be considered our kindred, but not now.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Perhaps there is someone who can answer our questions.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: ...Pope Yvangelista XI.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Move!
